$comment: Cross-book transcription rules for the textbook pipeline, grouped by subject kind, sitting between the generic contract template (textbook-contract.py) and each book's own observed cases. A clause is 'promoted' only when the same rule was observed in >= 2 different books (evidence lists them); 'seed' clauses are conservative, evidence-free starting points derived from transcribe-don't-correct and await confirmation.

clauses.rule: Kashida/tatweel (ـ) that stretches a word for justification or display is typography, not spelling: write the plain form (وفي, not وفــي). A stretched letter left unjoined before a space (بـــ س) keeps exactly one ـ so it keeps its connected shape. A difference in tatweel count is never a disagreement worth adjudicating.

Hamza is often omitted on alif (الاحصاء، الايثيل، الامشاج) and final ya drawn both dotted and dotless: transcribe each occurrence as drawn. One word may be spelled two ways on a page, or differ between caption, table and body — never unify them either way. Settle a tiny hamza on the native-density crop.

Transcribe exactly the harakat that are drawn: never supply a grammatically expected ending or tanwin, never strip a printed one, and keep the vowel that sits on a shadda as printed. Single fathas, dammas or shaddas below scan resolution are not adjudicable and are never marked illegible — keep the incumbent reading.

A bold body-size label at the margin that opens its own text (الحل :، مثال (١) :، أولاً :، العرض :) is a run-in label, never a heading. Only a centred line larger than the body (e.g. an exercise-set title) or one carrying section numbering takes `### `. Write them plain unless the book's observed section says it bolds them.

The long mid-height dash used in references (٢–٣), row and question numbers (١–), class intervals and exercise titles is an en dash – (U+2013), never an ASCII hyphen. A line that opens with a printed dash stays a text paragraph beginning with –, not a Markdown bullet; a printed • stays •.

Qur'anic quotations keep the book's own orthography — Uthmani rasm (ٱ، ۥ، ٰ، dotless ى), or a bare alif where the font drops a hamza — and its brackets, end-of-āyah ۝ (never ۞) and waqf marks as printed. Never restore or complete a verse from the mushaf. A waqf mark of unresolvable kind is left out, not chosen.

A table continued from the previous page that prints no header row gets an EMPTY Markdown header row; never repeat or compose one (الموضوع | الصفحة). If the header is re-printed partway down the page, the rows above it form their own table with an empty header — never hoist the header above them.

A table cell whose words wrap only because the column is narrow is one cell on one line, words joined by a space — no
, no extra row. Use
only when the cell prints two distinct stacked entries (a label over its symbol, two listed words), and never invent a separator between them.

Small print — an exponent inside a fraction, a footnote digit, a sukun, a one-letter figure label, digits in a rotated table — vanishes or misreads at page-render density. Read it on the native-density crop before writing it or marking it [غير مقروء]; a span the crop resolves is never illegible, nor is a whole legible grid.

Numeric glyphs are content: keep each decimal separator as drawn (Arabic ٫, comma or dot; with or without leading zero) even when mixed on one page, keep padding zeros, and keep the printed multiplication glyph (×, or a Latin X — never \times). A percent sign printed left of its number is written after it, spaced: ٩٠ ٪.

In a Latin-digit reference (section 2-5-3, figure, example, equation) the bidi engine can draw the parts in either visual order. Settle the order by hierarchy — which component is the chapter, checked against the chapter or lesson the page belongs to — on the native-density crop, never from glyph order on the page render.

Equations, products and matrices are set right to left: store the rightmost printed term first in the LaTeX source, and the rightmost printed matrix column is column 1. The rendered math looks mirrored against the page; that is expected — never reorder to the left-to-right convention. An identity or symmetric matrix cannot test this.

A stacked fraction (numerator over a rule) is \frac{}{}, never an inline solidus, and gains no parentheses the print lacks. Limits printed above and below Σ belong inside the math run as \sum_{…}^{…}, never as orphan text lines above and below the sentence; a Σ printed without limits stays bare.

A unit or chapter opener's decorative frame (arch, scroll, curl) is not a figure: transcribe only the printed title lines, with no image reference and no label list. If an opener carries a real uncaptioned illustration, its alt text is the bare word شكل, never a composed description.

The two hemistichs of a verse go on ONE Markdown line separated by plain spaces — no   or other HTML. The width of that gap is layout, not content, and is never a disagreement. Literal asterisks printed between hemistichs are escaped (\*\*) so they render as asterisks, not emphasis.

Words the print underlines — usually the ones an analysis or exercise refers to as «تحتها خطّ» — keep the underline as <u>…</u> around exactly the underlined word. Never substitute bold, never widen it to the whole line, and never drop it: the sentence that points at it then points at nothing.

A footnote call is the printed characters only — a raised Arabic-Indic digit in parentheses attached as printed (وَدَدا(١)) — never <sup>. Reproduce each call's inner and outer spacing as drawn, even when it varies on one page, and give the note at the page foot with the same marker.

Every verse or scripture quotation is read off the page, never quoted from memory or a reference text. Keep every printed diacritic and Uthmani mark, the ornamental brackets ﴿ ﴾ (or plain parentheses where those are printed) and the verse-number glyph as printed; a number you cannot read inside an ornament is [غير مقروء], not supplied.

Honorific formulas keep the printed form: a ligature glyph (ﷺ، رضي الله عنه as a single mark) stays the glyph, a spelled-out phrase stays spelled out, and an abbreviation (صلى الله عليه وسلم as (ص)) stays abbreviated. Never expand, contract or add one.

A hadith, its chain of narrators and its source citation (رواه البخاري) are transcribed verbatim in printed order, with the book's own brackets and punctuation. Never complete a truncated chain or text, and never add or correct a citation from another collection.

Pages read left to right, top to bottom; on two columns the left column is read fully first. Arabic glosses or instructions printed inside the page stay inline, in place, in their own script — never translated or moved to the end.

Keep the book's own spelling variety (British or American), accents and diacritics (é, à, ç, ï), apostrophes, quotation marks (" " ‘ ’ « ») and the spacing before French ; : ! ? exactly as printed. Never correct grammar, spelling or a missing accent in a reading passage or exercise.

Fill-in blanks are written as printed — a run of underscores (escaped \_ so Markdown keeps them) or dots, roughly the printed length — and are never filled in. Answer options (a) b) c)) and dialogue speaker labels keep their printed form and are not converted to Markdown list syntax.

A map is a figure: emit the image reference with its printed caption, then every printed place name, legend entry and scale label as a bullet in reading order. Never add a place the map does not print, and never describe what a region shows.

A timeline, chronology strip or arrow sequence of events is a figure or a list in reading order, not a Markdown table, unless the print draws a ruled grid. Each printed date stays with its event on one bullet.

Dates keep their printed calendar suffix and form (هـ / م, a range drawn ١٩٥٦–١٩٦٩) and are never converted between calendars or reconciled with another page. Personal, tribal and place names keep the printed spelling, even when it differs from a common form or from elsewhere in the book.

A quoted primary source — a treaty clause, a speech, a document excerpt — is transcribed verbatim with its printed quotation marks and attribution line; never complete or modernise it from a known version.
